thread.title: Cotton prices continue upward trend as USDA reports export sales data

author: Buckeye Reporter
title: Cotton prices continue upward trend as USDA reports export sales data
text:
Cotton futures continued to rise on April 18, with prices up between 60 and 75 points on Friday morning. The rally followed Thursday’s gains, when contracts closed between 11 and 71 points higher. Other commodities also saw movement, with the US dollar index increasing by $0.184 to $98.035 and crude oil rising by $1.90.
The latest data from the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) showed that a total of 161,101 running bales (RB) of old crop cotton were sold in the week ending April 9, marking the lowest figure in six weeks but still nearly 40 percent above sales during the same week last year. Vietnam was the leading buyer with purchases totaling 62,100 RB, while Turkey bought 49,000 RB. New crop sales reached 26,863 RB for the week; Vietnam again led purchases at 20,700 RB. Shipments for that period totaled 305,029 RB—a four-week low—with Vietnam receiving the largest share at over one-third of shipments.
Other market indicators included The Seam reporting sales of more than ten thousand bales at an average price just over seventy-two cents per pound on Wednesday. The Cotlook A Index dropped by twenty points to eighty-five point sixty cents per pound as of April fifteenth. ICE certified cotton stocks increased by nearly three thousand bales on April fifteenth to reach a level above one hundred sixty-two thousand bales. Meanwhile, the Adjusted World Price climbed another two hundred eighty-seven points on Thursday to sixty-one point sixty-one cents per pound.
May twenty-six cotton closed at seventy-five point seven cents—up fifty-nine points—and was trading up sixty-three points later in Friday’s session. July twenty-six and December twenty-six contracts also posted increases both at close and during morning trading.

The cooperative maintains facilities such as grain centers and agronomy sites throughout northwest Ohio and employs more than one hundred fifty people across its divisions according to its official website . Legacy Farmers Cooperative supports community initiatives including youth agricultural education programs like FFA and scholarships according to its official website .
Austin Schroeder did not hold any positions in securities mentioned in this article at publication time.
